equivalentMutants.name: inner join to address type made a left join (unknown address types kept)
equivalentMutants.reason: Under the source schema foreign key, every BusinessEntityAddress.AddressTypeID has a matching AddressType row, so changing this join from inner to left cannot affect an input satisfying the source preconditions.

objections.text: The hand-derived fixed cases already test a lowercase province code joining 'US' under CI_AS and a province code with a trailing space joining 'US'. Additional mixed-case spellings and combining case with the trailing space attack the same two join mechanisms.
objections.resolution: A01 now uses non-ASCII Latin-1 and Greek case pairs and puts the combined case/trailing-space variant on the country side, exercising Unicode folding and asymmetric trimming paths absent from the hand-derived inputs.

objections.text: A08 duplicates the exact BusinessEntityAddress primary-key tuple (vendor 1, address 1, address type 2). It also sends AddressType names 'Shipping' and 'SHIPPING', which collide under the source case-insensitive unique key. The duplicate fan-out input is not valid source data.
objections.resolution: A08 now uses three distinct BusinessEntityAddress primary-key tuples and distinct AddressType names. Its case-only pair crosses Vendor.Name and AddressType.Name, avoiding both unique constraints.

objections.text: A10 sends BusinessEntityAddress.AddressTypeID 9 without a matching AddressType row. The source foreign key requires that match, so the new case is outside the source schema preconditions. The inner-to-left-join mutant is unobservable for valid source inputs and is recorded in equivalentMutants instead.
